newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Kabila wants to appoint minister for refugee crisis.
newsitem.headline: Kabila wants to appoint minister for refugee crisis.

text.p: Congo President Laurent Kabila on Tuesday offered to appoint a minister to work with international agencies on repatriating Rwandan refugees, the United Nations reported.

Kabila, according to spokesman Fred Eckhard, suggested the plan in a private meeting with U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on the fringes of the Organisation of African Unity summit being held in the Zimbabwean capital, Harare.

Annan spoke to Kabila on the "plight of the refugees and the need for more cooperation with the humanitarian community (and) Kabila suggested a minister of his government to be the contact person for UNCHR," the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees office, Eckhard told a news briefing.

Kabila, the new president of the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire, also said he needed U.N. assistance for reconstruction, which Annan said he was willing to give. The secretary-general also urged him to broaden his government.
The refugees are remnants of 1.1 million Hutus who fled Rwanda in 1994 to escape reprisals for the genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
Some 814,807 have returned home since last November, while 46,300 have been found and 246,893 remain unaccounted for, according to UNHCR.
But in Kinshasa on Wednesday , a Cabinet minister said there was no evidence Rwandan Hutu refugees were being massacred in Congo as relief agencies have alleged.

"Whether it is an official of the United Nations or whoever that makes these allegations they should not be made lightly and without verification," Information Minister Raphael Ghenda said in answer to questions.
"The word massacre no longer carries the weight it once did, and for anybody to make allegations without evidence is pure and simple irresponsibility," Ghenda said.

Annan, in an earlier speech to the summit, said: "It is necessary even now that the protection of human life, the full respect of human life, is given the highest priority and that the rule of law should quickly return to that country."
